questions.question: Which of the following is a valid category of computer keyboard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**QWERTY**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **QWERTY**__ is a __**valid category of computer keyboard**__.

 __
 
• **QWERTY **is a keyboard layout for** Latin-script characters**.
 
• The name comes from the order of the **first six keys **on the** upper left letter row **of the** keyboard**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The** keyboard** is an input device.
 
• The keyboard is **similar **to an **electric typewriter**. 
 
• The keyboard uses a **serial port **to connect to the computer.
 
• The keyboard only **sends data **to a computer and does **not receive any information** from it.
 
• Keys on the keyboard are of mainly three types:
 
 
• **Alphanumeric keys**: Letters and numbers.
 
• **Punctuation keys**: comma, period, semicolon, etc.
 
• **Special keys**: Function keys, arrow keys, caps lock key, etc.

questions.question: Which linux distribution is derived from Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CentOS.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) is a Linux-based operating system that is designed for business**.
 
• It supports application development tools, automation protocols, cloud computing, middleware storage, management software etc. RHEL is the successor to Fedora Core.
 
• **It is a GNU distribution developed by Red Hat. Companies including Samsung Electronics, CIGNA Corporation, Cardinal Health Inc., and Toyota Motor North America uses RHEL**.
 
• Distribution systems of Linux include Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, centOS, Kali and Fedora.
 
• **CentOS stands for Community ENTerprise Operating System which allows you to develop, test and contribute to delivered distribution that tracks ahead of RHEL. Hence option 4 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fedora Linux is an open-source Linux-based operating system, designed for general purposes. It was initially released in 2003 as Fedora Core.**
 
• **Parrot OS is a Debian (Linux) based operating system designed for penetration testing, and ethical hacking.** It is lightweight and suitable for old hardware or limited resource systems.
 
• **Kali Linux (formerly BackTrack Linux) is an open-source Debian-based Linux distribution used for penetration testing and security auditing.** It has 600+ penetration testing or information security tools. That's why hackers normally use Kali Linux.

questions.question: Which of the following options enables the computer hardware to communicate with the computer software?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Operating System"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **operating system (OS)** is referred to as **system software**.
 
• The **boot program **helps the operating system for being initially loaded into the computer.
 
• The **operating system's main job **is to manage all of the other application programs as well as build the communication between hardware and software, in a system.
 
• It is also responsible for controlling **input and output**.
 
• The operating system also creates two operations, partitioning and logical formatting for using disk space to hold its files and folders.

**Thus the correct answer is** *"Operating system"*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RAM: **The word **RAM **stands for **Random Access Memory**. It is a very **fast internal memory **of the CPU. It holds data **temporarily.** After switching off the computer, data are deleted from the **RAM.** This characteristic is known as **volatility**. There are two types of RAM. These are SRAM and DRAM.
 
• **Microsoft Word: **It is referred to as **word processing software.** In MS Word, the user can** read, write or modify** the document. **MS Word** is mainly used for **writing reports, stories** and so on.
 
• **Motherboard: **The motherboard is referred to as a circuit board. It is responsible for building the connection between all the hardware to the processor. It also distributes electricity with the help of a power supply.

• 
 The word **RAT** is the abbreviation of **Remote Access Trojans**.
 
 
• 
 **Remote Access Trojans **are designed as **malware programs**.
 
 
•

• 
 Remote Access Trojan collects and uses the victim's information like usernames, passwords, screenshots, keystrokes, emails, chat lots, etc.

questions.question: Which storage medium has tracks and sectors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Hard Disk"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Pen drive:** The **pen drive **is recognised as a **USB drive**. It is also known as a flash drive or memory stick. It is mainly used for storing data and transferring the data as per the requirement. The size of the pen drive is small. That is why it is a very much portable device. The user can plug it into the USB port on the computing device. 
 
• **Hard disk: **The hard disk is the secondary storage device of the computing system. It is **non-volatile in nature**. The capacity of the space in the hard disk is huge. The hard disk has** tracks** and **sectors** for keeping the data.
 
• **Primary memory: **The primary is referred to as the main memory of the computer. RAM and ROM are the two types of main memory.
 
• **ROM: **The word** ROM** stands for **Read Only Memory**. It is **permanent memory **that the user will solely **read **but** cannot write of it.** This sort of memory is non-volatile. The data is kept for good in such recollections throughout manufacture. A memory stores such directions that square measure needed to begin a computing system. This operation is remarked as bootstrap. Memory chips don't seem to be solely utilized in the computing system however conjointly in different electronic things like cleaning machines and microwave ovens. MROM, PROM, EPROM and EEPROM are the types of ROM.

**Thus the correct answer is** *"Hard disk"*.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences can be used to delete the contents of a cell in an MS Excel worksheet?
questions.solution:
**The correct option is (3)**

Select -> Delete

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Click the arrow next to Delete in the Cells group on the Home tab, then select Delete Cells.
 
• Simply pick the cells you want to clear, then press Ctrl + Shift + Del on your keyboard to accomplish this. The selected cells' contents will be instantly cleared when you use this shortcut.
 
• Get rid of a worksheet

 Select with a right-click on the Sheet tab. Delete.

 Instead, you can choose the sheet first, then Home > Delete > Delete Sheet.
 
• The cells, columns, or rows that are chosen will be deleted if you press Ctrl + Delete. Shift + Delete: With this shortcut, you can delete a row, column, or set of cells while also moving the other cells to the right or left.
 
• Click Delete next to Remarks on the Review tab. As a hint, you can also remove a remark by using the close button in the comment balloon's upper right corner.
 
• Excel has two different cell deletion options: deleting just the cell's contents and deleting the entire cell. A cell, any selected row or group of rows, a random column, and the removal of formatting from a cell selection are all possible outcomes of the Delete operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Select -> Esc: This shortcut does not perform any function. "Select" is not a valid key on a keyboard and "Esc" usually means "Escape" which is used to cancel a command or operation.
 
• Select -> Ctrl Select: This shortcut is used to select multiple non-contiguous pieces of text. You can hold down the "Ctrl" key on your keyboard and then click on different parts of the text you want to select. This allows you to select text that is not in a continuous block.
 
• Select -> Delete: This shortcut is used to delete the currently selected text. Once you have selected the text you want to delete, pressing the "Delete" key on your keyboard will remove it from your document.
 
• Select -> Alt: This shortcut does not perform any function. "Select" is not a valid key on a keyboard and "Alt" is usually used as a modifier key to access menu items or perform other shortcuts.

questions.question: In Gmail, if you delete an email, it will be moved to the ________ folder.
questions.solution:
**The correct option is (2)**

Trash

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A message that you delete remains in your trash for 30 days. It will be permanently erased after that point.
 
• On Gmail and Google Apps, an archived message defaults to the Archive folder or All Mail while a deleted message goes into the trash folder.
 
• Your deleted emails can be automatically removed from your trash folder permanently depending on your email provider or company's policies

questions.question: What is a piece of code which is capable of copying itself and having a detrimental effect, such as corrupting an individual system or destroying its data?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Virus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A computer virus is a type o**f computer program that, **when executed,** replicates itself by modifying** other computer programs and inserting its own code into** those programs.**
 
• If this replication succeeds, the affected areas are then **said to be "infected" with a computer virus,** a metaphor derived from biological viruses.
 
• Computer **viruses generally require a host program.**
 
• The virus writes its own code into the** host program.**
 
• When the program runs, the written **virus program is executed first,** causing infection and damage.
 
• Worm, **ILOVEYOU, SQL Slammer, Stuxnet, **CryptoLocker, Tinba, Welchia, and Shlayer are some examples of computer viruses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
 

 **Trojan Horse**
 
 
 
• In computing, a Trojan horse is any **malware that misleads** users of its true intent. The term is derived from the** Ancient Greek story **of the deceptive Trojan Horse that led to the fall of the city of Troy.
 
 
 
 

 **Worm**
 
 
 
• A computer worm is a **standalone malware computer program** that replicates itself in order to spread to other computers. It often uses a computer network to spread itself, relying on **security failures** on the target computer to access it. It will use this machine as a** host to scan** and infect other computers. 
 
 
 
 

 **Zombies**
 
 
 
• In computing, a zombie is a computer **connected to the Internet** that has been compromised by a hacker via a computer virus, **computer worm**, or trojan horse program and can be used to** perform malicious tasks** under the remote direction of the hacker.

questions.question: Which among the following is full form of SMPS
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

__Switched Mode Power Supply (SMPS)__

 
• A switched-mode power supply (SMPS) is an electronic circuit that converts power using switching devices that are turned on and off at high frequencies, and storage components such as inductors or capacitors to supply power when the switching device is in its non-conduction state.
 
• Switching power supplies have high efficiency and are widely used in a variety of electronic equipment, including computers and other sensitive equipment requiring stable and efficient power supply.
 
• SMPS takes AC mains input and provides DC output (3.3V to 12V).
 
• The input DC supply from a rectifier or battery is fed to the inverter where it is turned on and off at high frequencies of between 20 KHz and 200 KHz by switching MOSFET or power transistors.
 
• The high-frequency voltage pulses from the inverter are fed to the transformer's primary winding, and the secondary AC output is rectified and smoothed to produce the required DC voltages.
 
• A feedback circuit monitors the output voltage and instructs the control circuit to adjust the duty cycle to maintain the output at the desired level.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.text: An input device sends information to a computer system for processing
An input device reproduces or displays the results after processing the data
An output device reproduces or displays the results after processing the data
Depending on the interaction, a device can work both as input and output, referred to as I/O device

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"****An input device reproduces or displays the results after processing the data"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **computer** is a **digital computing system** designed to perform all kinds of **arithmetic and logical operation**.
 
• The computer **receives** **input **either from the **user **or the data stored in the **memory, processes** it and produces the desired output. **Keyboard, mouse, touch-pen, scanner **etc. are examples of** input devices**.
 
• The output of the processed data is displayed at the respective output devices. Such as **monitors, printers, projector screens** and so on.
 
• Depending on the interaction, a device can work both as input and output, referred to as an I/O device.

**Thus the correct answer is** *"An input device reproduces or displays the results after processing the data".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word computer is derived from the word compute. In the year **1833, English mechanical engineer Charles Babbage** designed the first analytical engine. He is known as the **father of the computer.**
 
• In the beginning, computers are used for calculating large numbers and can only store a small amount of data.
 
• The **software** and the **hardware** parts of the computers are running together to execute the operations smoothly.
 
• **Software is a set of instructions or programs** given to the computers' hardware to perform a task. For example, system **software (OS), application software( MS Office, Browser)**, and **programming software(compiler)**.

questions.question: Select the smallest (computer) memory size?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kilobyte.**____ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The **K**ilobyte is the smallest unit of measurement greater than a byte.
 
• It precedes the megabyte, which contains 1,000,000 bytes, while one kilobyte is technically 1,000 bytes.
 
• Kilobytes are often used synonymously with kibibytes, which contain 1,024 bytes.
 
• Kilobyte (KB) = 1 KB = 1024 Bytes
 
• Megabyte (MB) = 1 MB = 1024 KB
 
• GigaByte (GB) = 1 GB = 1024 MB
 
• TeraByte (TB) = 1 TB = 1024 GB
 
• PetaByte (PB) = 1 PB = 1024 TB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The **memory unit** is the amount of data that can be stored in the storage unit.
 
• A group of **8 bits is called a byte.**
 
• A **byte **is the smallest unit, which can represent a data item or a character.

questions.question: A ________ is a software which is used to view websites.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Web browser**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A web browser is a software which is used to view websites**__. 

 __
 
• When a** user requests a web page** from a particular website, the** browser retrieves its files **from the** web server and then displays **the page on the **user's screen**. 
 
• Browsers are used on a range of devices including** desktops, laptops, tablets, **and **smartphones**.
 
• **Some commonly used web browsers are:**
 
 
• **Internet Explorer: **Internet Explorer (IE) is a web browser from Microsoft
 
• **Firefox: **Firefox is a free, open-source web browser from Mozilla
 
• **Google Chrome: **Google Chrome is a free, open-source web browser developed by Google
 
• **Opera:** Opera is a free, fast, small, and standard-compliant web browser developed by the Opera Software company
 
• **Netscape: **Netscape was the first commercial web browser
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **web page** is a **hypertext document** on the **World Wide Web**. 

 
 
• Web pages are delivered to the user by a web server and displayed in a web browser.
 
 
 
• A **web server **is computer software and the underlying hardware that accepts requests **via HTTP or its secure version HTTPS**.
 
• A** web spider **is a computer program used to search for and automatically index website content and other information on the Internet. 
 
 
• These programs, or bots, are commonly used to create entries for search engine indexes.
